title: HTML Drag and Drop API
summary: Move data between a draggable item and a drop target.

subtopics.title: Make an element draggable
subtopics.explanation: The `draggable` attribute opts a supported element into the browser’s drag-and-drop events. It does not by itself move data or update the page. For example, mark a card as draggable, then handle the drag events to describe what the user is carrying. Keep a keyboard-accessible way to perform the same action.

subtopics.title: Prepare data in dragstart
subtopics.explanation: The `dragstart` event fires when a drag begins. Put a small identifier or text value in `event.dataTransfer` so the eventual drop target knows what was selected. Avoid storing sensitive information there; the payload is for the interaction, not a secure data channel.

subtopics.title: Allow a valid drop target
subtopics.explanation: Browsers usually reject dropping by default. In a valid target’s `dragover` handler, call `event.preventDefault()` to allow the drop. Check whether the dragged item is acceptable before showing a drop indicator, so users are not invited to place data somewhere that cannot receive it.

subtopics.title: Handle the drop
subtopics.explanation: The `drop` event fires when the user releases the dragged item over an allowed target. Read the expected value from `dataTransfer`, validate it, and then update application state. For example, move a card only after confirming that the target column accepts that card type.

subtopics.title: Offer an accessible alternative
subtopics.explanation: Dragging can be difficult with touch, keyboard, or assistive technology. Offer another action, such as Move up/down buttons or a destination menu, that accomplishes the same task. Announce successful moves and keep focus predictable so the result is clear to everyone.

foundations.overview: The HTML Drag and Drop API provides events for dragging data and dropping it on a target. A drop target usually must prevent the dragover default behavior. Native drag interactions vary across devices, so provide buttons or menus as an alternative.
foundations.mentalModel: It is like carrying a labeled box from one marked station to another.
foundations.whyItMatters: It can support desktop workflows such as moving cards or files.

keyTakeaways: draggable enables native dragging for supported elements.
dragstart writes allowed data to dataTransfer.
drop reads the data and updates application state.
Provide a non-drag alternative and touch-friendly behavior.
